method: decimate 44.1k->2940 Hz (scipy FIR, zero-phase); 60 s Hann coherent FFT per block per channel with a 12 dB local-tonality gate (median over f+/-4..16 Hz) to reject the spoken guidance; carrier frequencies pinned by 240-1080 s Hann windows with quadratic log-interpolated peaks; levels by exact-frequency coherent DFT; every claimed beat re-verified by FFT of the analytic envelope of the band-passed mono sum. Same pipeline as the F10/F12/F15 run.
level_reference: level_db_rel is 20*log10(amplitude) relative to the strongest carrier anywhere in the track (the 49.75 Hz sub-delta member during 240-600 s). The track's overall level drops ~30 dB into the 900-1980 s deep section, so cross-section comparisons of level_db_rel reflect the master fade, not the layer mix; use levels_within_section for the mix.

track.file: Free Flow Journey in Focus 21 (personal copy, 2406.04 s)

transfer.verdict: NOT the 51.3 ppm-fast master. A single scale factor of 0.9999958 (-4.2 ppm) fits 30 measured tones to exactly round nominals with 0.004 Hz rms residual. Forcing F12's 1.0000513 gives 0.028 Hz rms - 7x worse - so the F12 speed error is rejected. F21 runs at correct speed, like F15. No de-scaling applied; the nominals below ARE the measured values to 0.015 Hz.

ntsc_pilot.note: The 15734 Hz NTSC line-rate pilot is present, so this master also passed through a video-based PCM adaptor - but at correct speed. The pilot is NOT constant: 15733.76 Hz for 0-300 s, a louder 15729.69 Hz for ~300-700 s, then 15734.17 Hz from 800 s to the end. The programme carriers show no matching shifts, so these are splice/transfer-source boundaries in the pilot itself, not speed changes in the audio.

polarity.convention: beat sign is positive when the RIGHT ear carries the high member
polarity.note: F21 swaps ear polarity once, early, during a ~15 s crossfade around 220 s, and never swaps back. This is the same trick F15 uses, but F21 does it at the intro/body seam rather than mid-session, and the whole 36-minute body is R-high.

mono_carriers.note: true mono anchor, in phase; beats 0.25 Hz against 49.75 in L and 0.50 Hz against 50.5 in R
UNEXPLAINED. Identical frequency in both ears (no beat), near-antiphase, 18 dB prominence, deep section only. Present in the 44.1 kHz original, so not a decimation artifact.

left_ear.198/248/298: 50 Hz apart - no audible monaural beat

same_channel_spacings.note: The only same-channel spacing slow enough to be heard as a monaural beat is the 50 Hz cluster: 0.25 Hz in the left ear, 0.50 Hz in the right, both against the shared 50.0 Hz anchor. Envelope demodulation of the cluster shows 0.252, 0.497 and 0.748 Hz at once - identical in structure to F12's, with the ears swapped.

structure.label: intro
structure.content: L-high 50.5/49.75 (0.75 Hz) and 100.75/99.25 (1.5 Hz) + mono 50.0; spoken guidance

structure.label: polarity crossfade
structure.content: both members present in both ears; L-high -> R-high

structure.label: descent
structure.content: R-high sub-delta 0.75 + delta 1.5 + theta 4.0 on 200/250/300 enter

structure.label: alpha bloom
structure.content: 10 Hz layer on 400/500/600 added over the theta stack; whole mix then fades ~30 dB

structure.label: handover
structure.content: sub-delta, delta and alpha drop out; 16 Hz beta layer fades in

structure.label: deep section (18 min)
structure.content: only 4 Hz theta (200/250/300) + 16 Hz beta (600/755/900 centres) + the unexplained 276.676 Hz mono tone

structure.label: return
structure.content: beta out; sub-delta, delta, theta and the 10 Hz alpha layer return, level rises

structure.label: exit signal
structure.content: 467/483 and 592/608 at 16 Hz plus 568/632 at 64 Hz, R-high, ramping up to the end

noise_bed.character: Brown-ish, not pink: -18.6 dB/decade over 200 Hz - 8 kHz (pink would be -10, brown -20), matching all three siblings. It IS surf: 28.9% envelope modulation in the 300-3000 Hz band against 9.2% for stationary Gaussian noise through the identical chain, peaking at 0.099 Hz (~10 s period). That is twice F12's surf depth and the slowest surf rate of the four tapes.
noise_bed.level_estimator: split: coherent full-window FFT carrier peak-above-local-median; Welch 2^17 bed continuum, tones excised 20 Hz-20 kHz
noise_bed.level_estimator_detail: Same ratio definition as bed-results.json's level_definition (tone-excised broadband continuum RMS over the strongest in-window carrier's RMS), but the two sides are measured with different estimators on purpose. The bed continuum is a Welch PSD (2^17 pt, 0.366 Hz bins here), because a continuum needs segment-averaging to be stable. The carrier is a single coherent line, so it is measured on one full-window Hann periodogram (0.0083 Hz bins over the 120 s window), peak-above-local-median with a +/-1-bin core and a +/-0.5-5 Hz sideband floor. Rationale: a coherent line's power stays in one or two bins at any resolution, while the continuum floor's power PER BIN is a density that shrinks as bins narrow -- so the identical real tone reads as indistinguishable from the floor at Welch's coarse bins (ratio 0.11x) and clears a >3x presence guard at full-window resolution (3.9x). Measuring both sides with one estimator conflates 'is this tone real' with 'how coarse is my continuum estimator'. See tests/test_bed_acceptance.py::_carrier_power_coherent, which implements exactly this split.
noise_bed.level_provenance: measured from the tape-era recording in a later calibration pass, separate from the original analysis pass

pan.depth_definition: peak-to-peak of the ILD trace, 97.5th minus 2.5th percentile
pan.method: Same direct pan measurement bed-results.json ran on F12/F15: ILD = 10*log10(E_L/E_R) on a 1.5-8 kHz band-passed pair, 250 ms hops (1 s windows for the depth figure), then the DFT of the resulting ILD trace. Depth is the trace's 97.5-2.5 percentile spread, which is the convention tests/test_noise.py::test_crossfade_ild_period_and_depth measures renders with. Period refined by least-squares sinusoid fit over a frequency grid.
pan.one_x_not_two_x: SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT, not by analogy. The ILD trace carries a line at 0.1009-0.1010 Hz standing 70x (120 s window) to 235x (1080 s window) over its local spectral median, with H2/H1 = 0.09-0.10 and H3/H1 = 0.008. A least-squares sinusoid fit at HALF that rate (0.0505 Hz, 19.8 s) recovers an amplitude of 0.004-0.018 dB against the fundamental's 1.16-1.46 dB, i.e. under 1.5% -- there is no 20 s component. So the LFO fundamental is ~9.90 s and f21-results' 0.099 Hz envelope-swell peak is that fundamental (F15's arrangement), NOT its second harmonic (F12's arrangement, where the swell sits at 2*f0). The 20.2 s reading the F12 analogy would have implied is excluded outright. Per-channel (L and R separately) and mono-sum envelope spectra in the 300-3000 Hz bed band independently peak at the same 0.1009-0.1010 Hz with no half-rate line.
pan.depth_stability: 97.5-2.5 percentile p-p over five disjoint 120 s windows in the 1100-1880 s voice-free stretch: 2.830, 2.859, 2.842, 2.823, 2.848 dB (spread 0.04 dB). Sinusoid-fit p-p on the same windows: 2.67-2.71 dB. The percentile figure is the one presets are written against.
pan.coherence_in_bed_band: 0.003-0.013 from 250 Hz to 8 kHz on the 1200-1320 s window -- fully decorrelated, two independent noise streams, same construction as F12/F15.
pan.provenance: measured from the tape-era recording in a later calibration pass, separate from the original analysis pass. Supersedes the earlier inference (10.1 s / 3.5 dB) that read the period off the 0.099 Hz envelope peak and borrowed a depth by analogy with F12/F15.

noise_bed.level_robust_convention: physical bed power (Welch density x bin width, making the 44.1 kHz tape and 48 kHz renders comparable) over the coherent-FFT carrier power; carrier = mean over multiple disjoint 120 s windows
noise_bed.level_robust_detail: The single-window figure (18.3 dB at 1200-1320 s) is a phase-lottery reading: the 50.4987 Hz reference only stands ~4x over the brown bed's local floor in a +/-1-bin core, so a single 120 s coherent window reads |tone + that window's noise|^2 and swings +/-3 dB with the tone's phase against the noise. (A pure oscillator-phase change on the render side moves the reading 3.1 dB with no level change anywhere.) Six 120 s windows across the voice-free 1100-1820 s stretch read 18.98/18.04/26.52/31.97/19.86/19.65 dB in the old single-window convention; the 26.5/32.0 outliers are wow casualties (the line drifts +/-35 mHz per 10 s by complex demodulation, smearing it across several 8.3 mHz bins in an unlucky window; their presence guards collapse to 0.5x/0.04x vs 2.7-3.4x in the clean windows), not level changes. Target = mean of the four clean windows: carrier 1.27555e-05, physical bed 3.46634e-04, ratio 14.34 dB. bed_level_rms_rel_db above records the single-window reading; presets and the acceptance test calibrate against the robust figure.
noise_bed.level_robust_provenance: measured from the tape-era recording in a later calibration pass; supersedes bed_level_rms_rel_db for calibration purposes

49.75/50.5.note: isolated from the 50.0 mono anchor; the un-notched 50-cluster envelope shows 0.252, 0.497 and 0.748 Hz simultaneously

568/632.note: isolated with two 8 Hz band-passes; the naive wide band-pass also passes 592/608 and reads 40 Hz

anomalies.name: 276.676 Hz mono tone
anomalies.detail: Deep section only (900-1980 s). Identical to 0.0001 Hz in both ears so it produces no binaural beat, near-antiphase (L/R phase -166 deg), 18 dB above the local floor, about -32 dB relative to the section's strongest tone. Confirmed present in the 44.1 kHz original, so not a decimation artifact. It is on no round grid and is not an intermodulation product of anything present. Unexplained, reported as measured.

anomalies.name: 60 Hz mains harmonics
anomalies.detail: Tones at 60, 120, 180, 240 and 360 Hz are present, with 120 Hz the strongest (up to -8 dB relative in quiet passages) and identical in both channels at a fixed ~-110 deg interchannel phase. These are NOT programme: the 120 Hz component wanders by 101 ppm over the session while genuine carriers hold to 5.8 ppm. Mains hum from the transfer chain. Note the 240 Hz member is strong enough to survive naive peak-picking and look like a carrier.

anomalies.name: beta2 centre is 755, not 750
anomalies.detail: The middle 16 Hz pair measures 747.000/763.000 Hz, a centre of 755 Hz. The other two beta centres are exactly 600 and 900. 755 breaks the otherwise perfect round-number grid and is not the arithmetic midpoint (750). Held to 0.005 Hz for 18 minutes, so it is deliberate.

anomalies.name: level_db_rel spans a 30 dB master fade
anomalies.detail: The whole mix drops ~30 dB entering the deep section and comes back. Absolute levels therefore under-report the deep layers badly; the 16 Hz beta layer is the loudest thing in its own section despite reading -40 to -55 dB globally.

folklore_comparison.premise: Community folklore for Focus 21 claims ~4 Hz beats on low carriers plus ~16 Hz beta on 600/750/900 Hz carriers. Measured first, compared second.
agrees: 4 Hz on low carriers: EXACT. 198/202, 248/252 and 298/302, all beating 4.001 Hz measured, running 230-2260 s. This is the track's spine.
A 16 Hz beta layer exists: EXACT. Three pairs, 16.000 Hz measured on all three, holding for the entire 18-minute deep section.
This is the first of the four tapes where the folklore's headline claim is essentially correct.
disagrees: The middle beta carrier is 755 Hz, not 750: measured 747.000/763.000, held to 0.005 Hz over 18 minutes. Off by 5 Hz - small, but not a rounding of 750.
Folklore says nothing about the 10 Hz alpha layer on 400/500/600 (395/405, 495/505, 595/605), which runs 600-840 s and again 1980-2280 s.
Folklore says nothing about the 1.5 Hz delta pair (99.25/100.75) or the 0.75 Hz sub-delta pair (49.75/50.5), which together are the LOUDEST elements in the track - 30 dB above the theta layer.
Folklore says nothing about the mono 50.0 Hz anchor, or the 0.25/0.50/0.75 Hz monaural+binaural cluster it creates - the same construction as F12 with the ears swapped.
Folklore says nothing about ear polarity, nor about the L-high -> R-high flip at ~220 s. Reproduce F21 L-high and every beat in it is inverted relative to the tape.
Folklore says nothing about the 64 Hz exit pair (568/632) or the 467/483 exit pair, both in the final 70 seconds.
Folklore implies the 4 Hz and 16 Hz layers coexist throughout. They only overlap during 900-1980 s; the 16 Hz layer is absent from the first 15 minutes and the last 7.

our_reconstruction_comparison.preset: the project's pre-measurement focus-21 reconstruction preset (since removed; the bundled focus-21 is now built from this file's tables)
our_reconstruction_comparison.claims: 1.5 Hz delta core on a 200 Hz base (3 stacked pairs) gliding in from 6 Hz, plus a 40 Hz gamma accent on a 300 Hz base at -18 dB; pink bed at -20 dB; emerge to 15 Hz.
right: 1.5 Hz IS a real F21 beat and IS a core element - 99.25/100.75, present for essentially the whole track and among the two loudest layers. Good call.
Making the delta the dominant layer by level is correct: the 50 Hz and 100 Hz pairs sit 27-35 dB above the theta and beta layers.
Layering a fast 'heightened awareness' accent under a slow core is the right architecture. The tape does exactly this - it just uses 16 Hz, not 40.
Emerging on a beta-band beat is right in spirit: the tape's exit signal is 16 Hz (plus 64 Hz).
wrong: The 40 Hz gamma accent does not exist. Nothing in F21 beats at 40 Hz. The tape's fast accent is 16.000 Hz on three pairs. (Ironically a naive wide band-pass across 568-632 reads 40 Hz - an artifact of the 64 Hz pair overlapping the 16 Hz one, not a real beat.)

The accent is 18 dB down in our preset; on the tape the 16 Hz layer is the ONLY fast element and dominates its own 18-minute section, with the delta core removed entirely for the duration. The tape hands over; we crossfade under.
Our 1.5 Hz core sits on a 200 Hz base with 3 stacked pairs. The tape's 1.5 Hz pair is a single pair at 99.25/100.75, and 200 Hz is where the tape puts its 4 Hz theta instead.
Missing entirely: the 4 Hz theta spine on 200/250/300 that runs 34 of the 40 minutes; the 10 Hz alpha layer; the 0.75 Hz sub-delta pair; the mono 50 Hz anchor.
The 6.0 -> 1.5 Hz opening glide is invented. F21 has no glides at all: every carrier is bit-stable to a few ppm and layers enter and leave by crossfade, not by sliding.
Our bed is pink at -20 dB. The tape's bed is brown-ish (-18.6 dB/decade) and heavily surf-modulated (28.9% at 0.099 Hz). Wrong colour and no surf.
No ear-polarity handling, so we cannot express the L-high intro or the R-high body.
Emerge target 15 Hz vs the tape's 16 Hz plus an unmentioned 64 Hz burst - close on one, silent on the other.
our_reconstruction_comparison.verdict: Our reconstruction got the delta core right by reasoning and got the fast accent wrong by a factor of 2.5. The community folklore, which we treated as less reliable, is the more accurate of the two for this track: it names 4 Hz, 16 Hz and two of the three beta carriers exactly.

confidence_notes: All 14 pairs verified by independent envelope demodulation of the mono sum; every measured beat is within 0.021 Hz of nominal and no pair failed.
Carrier frequencies are good to +/-0.005 Hz (240-1080 s coherent windows).

The 64 Hz exit pair and the 0.75 Hz sub-delta pair required isolating band-passes; naive wide bands read 40 Hz and 0.50 Hz respectively because of overlapping neighbours. Both artifacts are documented above.
Section boundaries are quoted to the nearest 2-minute timeline block except the polarity flip (20 s windows) and the exit signal (15 s windows).
The 276.676 Hz tone is reported as measured with no explanation offered.
